scope: 225 fresh synthetic-fixture worker processes in four preregistered exploratory comparisons. Five cycles per workload and mode; alternating forward/reverse mode order. No agent builds, tests or scans overlap each cohort. Each cohort retains its separate controls; comparisons across cohorts are descriptive only.

protocol.reason: The prior post-native all-synchronous CAS probe reduced concurrent CPU 9 percent but regressed latency 13 percent. Separate metadata, reads and raw temporary writes to locate this tradeoff before deciding whether any production change is justified.
limitations: Source-module loader substitutions do not qualify distributed artifacts or frozen resource gates.
Only bounded scratch fixture on current local APFS; no production adoption or safety/responsiveness claim.
CAS read growth and remote-filesystem blocking remain unqualified; any candidate needs bounded safe reader and platform strategy.
All synchronization remains asynchronous and equally strong; exact event counts and full integrity required.
Every variant modifies source-module loading in memory; this is not a comparison of actual installed distribution entrypoints.
Only the 4096-byte profile, two warmups and ten noncold samples are used; cold has one timed sample. This is not the frozen 380-worker resource qualification.
Five process replicates do not establish confidence or broad performance acceptance. Reported means are exploratory; all original latency, CPU, process, RSS and storage gates remain unchanged.
Small synchronous I/O probes cover only controlled local fixture files. Growth, remote-filesystem stalls, generic streams and failure cleanup are not qualified for production.
Semantic validity, exact event counts and full integrity pass in every worker; these are fixture assertions, not human-reviewed quality or provider acceptance.
No provider calls, production activation, service change, publication or release-readiness claim.
decision: Retain current runtime. Fresh-row prefix serialization and sealed initial-borrow sharing have mixed small effects and cold regression. Callback-backed I/O provides no consistent improvement. Coarse synchronous CAS lowers concurrent CPU but raises latency; separating phases finds only a small read-only gain with cold regression. Do not rerun the same candidates without a new causal hypothesis. Continue from attribution of non-main-thread recording CPU, durable-write admission and exact distribution measurement ownership.
